title: Relative-spectrum characterization of quasi-affine morphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Say that $f$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] when for every affine open $U\subseteq S$, the open subscheme $f^{-1}(U)$ is isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Then $f$ is quasi-affine if and only if there exist a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebra $\mathcal A$ (a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]), and a quasi-compact open immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where $\pi:Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)\to S$ is the relative spectrum [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec], such that $\pi\circ i=f$.

proof.text: Assume $f$ is quasi-affine. For every affine open $U\subseteq S$, put $X_U=f^{-1}(U)$. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], $X_U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus $f$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It is also quasi-separated: [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $f_U:X_U\to U$ quasi-separated since its source is quasi-separated. The open subschemes $V_U=X_U\times_U X_U$ cover $X\times_S X$: a pair over a point $s$ belongs to $V_U$ whenever $s\in U$. The inverse image of $V_U$ under $\Delta_f$ is $X_U$, and the restricted diagonal is $\Delta_{f_U}$, because both components are the identity on $X_U$. These restricted diagonals are quasi-compact by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Apply [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] to the cover $(V_U)_U$ and $\Delta_f$. It follows that $\Delta_f$ is quasi-compact, which is precisely quasi-separatedness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (4): quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness; Schemes Tags 01K4 and 01KO

proof.text: Set $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_X$. The structure sheaf is quasi-coherent: on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ it is the associated sheaf $\widetilde R$, as in [pqf-def-coherent]. Step 1 supplies both hypotheses of [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh], so the underlying module of $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent. Its ring multiplication and its $\mathcal O_S$-algebra structure are those of the direct-image structure sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2). Obtain the affine morphism $\pi:Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)\to S$ and an algebra isomorphism $a:\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_*\mathcal O_Y$. For every affine open $U\subseteq S$, put $Y_U=\pi^{-1}(U)$; the chart $h_U:Y_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ has section map $a_U$.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (4): construction of the algebra and relative spectrum; Schemes Tag 01LC and Constructions Tag 01LX

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-algebra-local-maps] with $g=\pi$ and the algebra map $a^{-1}:\pi_*\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$. This is allowed because $\pi$ is affine; no affineness of $X$ or of an overlap is required. It gives maps $k_U:X_U\to Y$ over $S$ agreeing on every overlap. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], they glue to $c:X\to Y$. Their composites with $\pi$ agree with $f$ on every $X_U$, so uniqueness in that same gluing theorem gives $\pi c=f$. Each $k_U$ factors through the open $Y_U$, since its composite to $S$ has image in $U$; denote the resulting map by $c_U:X_U\to Y_U$. This factorization simply restricts the continuous map and the sheaf map to the indicated open subscheme. The section formula in the local-maps node says that $c_U$ induces $a_U^{-1}:\Gamma(Y_U,\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal A(U)=\Gamma(X_U,\mathcal O_X)$. Hence $h_Uc_U:X_U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X_U,\mathcal O_X)$ induces $a_U^{-1}a_U=\mathrm{id}$. Injectivity of the correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] identifies this composite with the canonical map defined by the identity on global sections. This is the affine-restriction description of the canonical map in Constructions Tag 01LY, now constructed from existing DAG statements.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (4): canonical morphism; Constructions Tag 01LY, lemma-canonical-morphism, with Tag 01LT

proof.text: Every $X_U$ is quasi-affine, so [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding] makes its canonical map to $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X_U,\mathcal O_X)$ an open immersion. Step 3 identifies this with $h_Uc_U$; since $h_U$ is an isomorphism, $c_U$ is an open immersion. By [def-weil-open-immersion], composing with the inclusion of $Y_U$ into $Y$ is again an open immersion: the composite identifies $X_U$ with an open subset of the open subset $Y_U$ and its sheaf map is a composite of isomorphisms. Also $c$ is injective on points: if $c(x)=c(x')=y$, choose an affine open $U$ containing $\pi(y)$. Then $x,x'\in X_U$, and injectivity of $c_U$ gives $x=x'$. The opens $X_U$ cover $X$, and their maps into $Y$ are the just-checked open immersions. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-injective-local-source] applies and makes $c$ an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (4): canonical map is an open immersion, using Properties Tag 01P9

proof.text: The open immersion $c$ is quasi-compact as a morphism, even when $S$ itself is not quasi-compact. Indeed the affine opens $U\subseteq S$ give an open cover $(Y_U)_U$ of $Y$, and $c^{-1}(Y_U)=X_U$ by $\pi c=f$. The scheme $X_U$ is quasi-compact by step 1 and $Y_U$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2), hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) to obtain quasi-compactness of $c_U:X_U\to Y_U$. Then [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] makes $c$ quasi-compact. Taking $i=c$ proves the required factorization in the forward direction.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, end of (2) implies (4): quasi-compactness of the canonical open immersion

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $\mathcal A,\pi:Y\to S,i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ satisfy the stated factorization. For any affine open $U\subseteq S$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2) identifies $Y_U=\pi^{-1}(U)$ with an affine scheme. The equation $\pi i=f$ gives $f^{-1}(U)=i^{-1}(Y_U)$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], restricting $i$ identifies this scheme with an open subscheme of $Y_U$. Because $Y_U$ is an affine open of $Y$, quasi-compactness of $i$, in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], says exactly that $i^{-1}(Y_U)$ is quasi-compact. Thus $f^{-1}(U)$ is isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. This holds for every affine open $U$, and hence $f$ is quasi-affine by [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] with the meaning specified in the item.

The opens X_U x_U X_U cover X x_S X, so the diagonal is quasi-compact by quasi-compactness local on the target. Step 2: f_*O_X is quasi-coherent by the qcqs pushforward lemma, and relative-spec (2) gives charts h_U whose section maps are a_U. Step 3: local-maps (any source) with alpha=a^{-1}, then gluing; uniqueness gives pi c = f. Checked (h_U c_U)^# = a_U^{-1} a_U = id, so h_U c_U is the canonical map j of X_U. Step 4: c is an open immersion via the injective-local-source lemma; injectivity is checked inside one affine U. Step 5: c is quasi-compact because X_U is quasi-compact and Y_U affine, then local on target; no quasi-compactness of S used. Step 6: the converse is elementary from relative-spec (2) and the definitions. Edge cases checked: empty X or S, identity, punctured A^2, non-quasi-compact S.
